lesson: Today we work on one technique, the exit. That means the poem ends on a picture of something you can see, not on a sentence that tells you what to think. Watch the last full lines before the close. The poem gives you one field coming clear, then the next, then the stone wall past it, then the whole grey morning loosens its grip and lets you through. Then it stops on the coffee. That first slow sip is worth crossing the room for. It does not sum anything up. It shows you a thing and quits. This works in a plain way. A picture stays in your head longer than a statement does. You leave holding the field and the coffee, so the poem keeps going in you after the word stop. Try this. End on one thing a person could point at and delete any line that explains it. The second time through, wait for the coffee and let so up move you.
